title.source: Seiko45萬的錶，為何還得回廠調整？｜品牌故事
title.text: Seiko: Why did a ¥450,000 watch still need factory adjustment? | Brand Stories

description.source:
一支新石英錶能走得準，為什麼仍可能回廠調整？從1960年代末顯微鏡下的手焊基板，沿著振子與馬達的小型化、1969年出貨改價、老化與爐溫現場檢查，走到後期分頻晶片，以及1977技術文裡的可維修接法。

上市與製程事件依精工／Epson回顧、2004企業史摘錄、2017青木茂技術史及1977安川英昭論文，各守時期與歸屬。沒有把多件回廠錶拼成一支可追蹤序號案例；兩成是振子初期良率，一成是特定階段IC挑選比例，並非退貨率。精度保留常溫條件；汽車價只比較1966東京卡羅拉Standard。初代hybrid、35SQ外購Intersil分頻晶片、自研A型與1971年12月38系，以及1977實裝，各守機種與時期。舊題瑞士產業單因果與全球免費專利說法不採。圖為匿名概念插畫。

description.text:
Why could a new quartz watch keep accurate time yet still need to go back to the factory for adjustment? We follow hand-soldered boards under microscopes in the late 1960s, smaller resonators and motors, the 1969 shipment and price change, aging and furnace checks, then later divider chips and repairable connections described in a 1977 technical paper.

Launch and manufacturing events follow Seiko/Epson retrospectives, excerpts from the 2004 company history, Shigeru Aoki's 2017 technical history and Hideaki Yasukawa's 1977 paper, preserving each period and attribution. Multiple returned watches are not combined into one traceable serial-number case. The 20% figure is early resonator production yield; 10% is the usable IC selection proportion at a particular stage, not a return rate. Accuracy retains its normal-temperature conditions; the car-price comparison uses only the 1966 Tokyo Corolla Standard. The initial hybrid circuit, the purchased Intersil divider chip for the 35SQ, the in-house Type A and December 1971 38 series, and the assembly described in 1977 remain distinct in model and period. We do not adopt the old single-cause account of Swiss industry or the claim of free patents worldwide. Images are anonymous conceptual illustrations.

skr1h02: 這是精工企業史記下的早期難題；
六〇年代末，技能者還在顯微鏡下手焊電路。
skr1e26: 你若只看錶面，看到的是秒針一格一格前進；
裡面的零件卻沒有排成一團。
skr1p14: 回到準備中的價牌，企業史說，
服部正次當晚到場，看過後要求改回四十五萬。
skr1f11: 這個事件讓現場檢查、留下記錄、
寫明作業步驟，成了工廠要記住的教訓。
skr1c22: 後來換上外購Intersil晶片，整套電路都換了嗎？
skr1d18: 我的答案是：準確要交到下一個人手上，
還得把穩定、製造與維修一起做好。
skr1d19: 留言告訴我，你選一件新工具時，
最想少操心的，是準確、維修，還是價格？

lines.source: 一九六九年，若你花四十五萬日圓買錶，仍可能需要送回調整。
lines.text: In 1969, even if you spent ¥450,000 on a watch, you might still have to send it back for adjustment.

lines.source: 這是精工企業史記下的早期難題；六〇年代末，技能者還在顯微鏡下手焊電路。
lines.text: Seiko's company history records this early problem; in the late 1960s, skilled workers were still hand-soldering circuits under microscopes.

lines.source: 陶瓷板上的電路，還得跟電池與齒輪，一起裝進小小的機芯。
lines.text: The circuit on a ceramic board had to fit into a tiny movement alongside the battery and gears.

lines.source: 我先盯著那支烙鐵：做出一支以後，下一支能同樣做出來嗎？
lines.text: I focus first on that soldering iron: after making one watch, could they make the next one the same way?

lines.source: 一張價牌，為什麼會讓上市前的準備突然改動？
lines.text: Why would a price tag suddenly change the preparations for launch?

lines.source: 而工廠的一座真空爐，又藏著什麼沒被記下的事？
lines.text: And what unrecorded detail lay hidden in a vacuum furnace at the factory?

lines.source: 跟著精工的Astron，從一塊手焊基板，追一支新錶如何走向持續製造。
lines.text: Follow Seiko's Astron from a hand-soldered board to see how a new watch moved toward sustained production.

lines.source: 把準確塞進手腕以後，還差哪些事，才能交給下一個人？
lines.text: Once accuracy fits on a wrist, what else must be done before handing it to the next person?

lines.source: 要交出去的，是你走路、抬手，還會換電池的腕錶。
lines.text: What you hand over is a wristwatch that moves as you walk and raise your arm, and whose battery you will replace.

lines.source: 先看最裡面的振子；它在這裡，負責給電路穩定的節拍。
lines.text: Start with the resonator deep inside; here, it gives the circuit a steady beat.

lines.source: 二〇一七年的技術史回顧記下，團隊選了音叉形的水晶。
lines.text: A 2017 technical history records that the team chose tuning-fork-shaped quartz.

lines.source: 當時市面上找不到適合腕錶的現成振子，團隊得自己試著加工。
lines.text: No ready-made resonator suitable for a wristwatch was available on the market then, so the team had to try machining one themselves.

lines.source: 技術史寫，他們試過研磨劑與振動，最後用磨石作出音叉形狀。
lines.text: The technical history says they tried abrasives and vibration, and finally made the tuning-fork shape using a grinding stone.

lines.source: 可是，把一塊水晶縮小，會不會連別的地方也得跟著改？
lines.text: But if you shrink a piece of quartz, will other parts have to change too?

lines.source: 回顧說，尺寸與振動頻率相連；做得更小，頻率會更高。
lines.text: The retrospective says size and vibration frequency are linked: smaller means a higher frequency.

lines.source: 振動變快，分頻回路的級數也會增加，耗電就跟著成為難題。
lines.text: Faster vibration calls for more frequency-divider stages, making power consumption a problem too.

lines.source: 當時這一款採用的，是每秒八千一百九十二次振動。
lines.text: This model at the time used 8,192 vibrations per second.

lines.source: 你手上的錶會晃動，那小振子總不能在裡面任意撞。
lines.text: The watch on your wrist moves around, so the little resonator cannot be allowed to knock about inside.

lines.source: 技術史的圖裡，它被細彈簧吊著，浮在真空封住的小膠囊中。
lines.text: In the technical history's diagram, thin springs suspend it inside a small vacuum-sealed capsule.

lines.source: 我看著那幾根細線，反而想問：節拍穩了，指針就能自己走嗎？
lines.text: Looking at those fine wires, I want to ask: once the beat is steady, can the hands move on their own?

lines.source: 還得把快節拍往下分，最後交出一秒一次的驅動訊號。
lines.text: That fast beat still has to be divided down to deliver a drive signal once per second.

lines.source: 這個設計用十三級分頻，每一級都把前面的頻率減半。
lines.text: This design uses 13 divider stages, each halving the frequency from the previous stage.

lines.source: 可是，這些回路當時靠什麼裝進去？
lines.text: But how did they fit those circuits inside at the time?

lines.source: 精工的產品史記下，電路包含七十六個電晶體、二十九個電容等零件。
lines.text: Seiko's product history records a circuit with 76 transistors, 29 capacitors and other components.

lines.source: 發振、分頻與驅動電路，組成了混合電路。
lines.text: The oscillator, divider and drive circuits formed a hybrid circuit.

lines.source: 你可以想像，手上那個細小接點，焊好後還要接著做下一個。
lines.text: Imagine soldering that tiny contact in your hand, then moving on to the next one.

lines.source: 但電路送出訊號，跟真的推動指針，中間還隔著一個馬達。
lines.text: But between the circuit sending a signal and the hands actually moving, there is still a motor.

lines.source: 馬達若一直耗電，腕上的小電池要怎麼撐住？
lines.text: If the motor draws power continuously, how can the little battery on your wrist last?

lines.source: 技術史回述，團隊曾把三片兩極磁鐵，按六十度間隔展開。
lines.text: The technical history recounts how the team arranged three two-pole magnets at 60-degree intervals.

lines.source: 他們送進驅動脈衝，看見磁鐵轉動；再試著縮短通電的時間。
lines.text: They applied drive pulses and saw the magnets turn, then tried shortening the time the power was on.

lines.source: 線圈也得跟著縮：大約兩萬圈，繞的是直徑零點零二毫米的細線。
lines.text: The coil had to shrink too: about 20,000 turns of fine wire just 0.02 millimeters in diameter.

lines.source: 你把這些纏好的線放回機芯，還得留下讓其他零件安放的位置。
lines.text: When you put that wound wire back in the movement, you still need space for the other components.

lines.source: 後來的六極馬達，一秒只短暫通電一次，轉子每步走六十度。
lines.text: The later six-pole motor received just one brief pulse per second, and its rotor moved 60 degrees per step.

lines.source: 通電讓它轉，那不通電的時候，轉子會不會自己滑走？
lines.text: Power makes it turn, but when the power is off, could the rotor slip out of position?

lines.source: 電流停下，轉子與定子間的吸引力，也幫忙把位置留住。
lines.text: When the current stops, attraction between the rotor and stator also helps hold it in place.

lines.source: 我會在意，這回要付出的不是轉得多快，而是每一步用了多少電。
lines.text: What interests me here is the cost in power of each step, rather than how fast it turns.

lines.source: 可馬達有了，整個放進小錶裡，還有地方嗎？
lines.text: But with the motor ready, is there room to fit the whole thing inside a small watch?

lines.source: 工程者把能分開的功能件拆開，讓線圈、定子與轉子，分散在機芯空隙。
lines.text: The engineers separated the functional parts they could, distributing the coil, stator and rotor through gaps in the movement.

lines.source: 你若只看錶面，看到的是秒針一格一格前進；裡面的零件卻沒有排成一團。
lines.text: If you only look at the dial, you see the second hand advance step by step; the components inside are spread out.

lines.source: 省下空間以後，機芯能收進圓形的外框；精工資料列外徑三十毫米。
lines.text: With space saved, the movement could fit within a round frame; Seiko's data lists an outside diameter of 30 millimeters.

lines.source: 但那是機芯的尺寸，電池所在的位置，還會比其他地方厚。
lines.text: But that is the movement's size, and the section containing the battery is thicker than the rest.

lines.source: 真要換電池時，你又得從哪裡打開？
lines.text: When it is time to change the battery, where do you open it?

lines.source: 精工產品史特別提到，採用電池蓋形式，讓更換比較容易。
lines.text: Seiko's product history specifically mentions a battery-hatch design that made replacement easier.

lines.source: 所以，工作台上的這套東西，哪一天才能真的送出去？
lines.text: So when could this assembly on the workbench actually be sent out?

lines.source: 送出之前，還得讓每一支能完成最後調整。
lines.text: Before shipping, each watch still had to be ready for its final adjustment.

lines.source: 企業史把下一個場景，記在一九六九年十二月二十四日。
lines.text: The company history dates the next scene to December 24, 1969.

lines.source: 技術主管安川英昭趕往東京時，十支水晶腕錶已經送出。
lines.text: As technical manager Hideaki Yasukawa hurried to Tokyo, ten quartz wristwatches had already been sent out.

lines.source: 另十支，安排隔天早上以前送到；留在工廠的工作還沒有結束。
lines.text: Another ten were scheduled to arrive by the next morning; work at the factory was still unfinished.

lines.source: 我原本以為這像一場早就排好的聖誕上市，回顧卻說，並不是。
lines.text: I had thought this was a Christmas launch planned well in advance, but the retrospective says it was not.

lines.source: 是做到這時候，才終於有望湊齊數量。
lines.text: Only at this point did there finally seem to be a chance of assembling enough watches.

lines.source: 如果你在準備明天的發表，錶到了，價牌是不是就能照印好的放？
lines.text: If you were preparing tomorrow's presentation and the watches had arrived, could you simply put out the printed price tags?

lines.source: 回顧說，銷售負責人一度把售價改成三十八萬日圓。
lines.text: The retrospective says the sales manager briefly changed the price to ¥380,000.

lines.source: 他覺得，能買一台大眾車的價錢，實在太高。
lines.text: He felt that a price high enough to buy a mass-market car was simply too much.

lines.source: 這個尺度有多大？你得先看是哪一年、哪個等級的車。
lines.text: How much money was that? First, you need to check the car's year and trim level.

lines.source: 豐田在一九六六年公布，東京的卡羅拉標準型，售價四十三萬二千日圓。
lines.text: In 1966, Toyota announced a Tokyo price of ¥432,000 for the Corolla Standard.

lines.source: 同張表上的豪華型，則是四十九萬五千日圓。
lines.text: The Deluxe on the same price list was ¥495,000.

lines.source: 同一支錶，銷售端改過價格，最後又是誰來拍板？
lines.text: For the same watch, sales had changed the price, but who would make the final decision?

lines.source: 回到準備中的價牌，企業史說，服部正次當晚到場，看過後要求改回四十五萬。
lines.text: Back at the price tags being prepared, the company history says Shoji Hattori arrived that evening, looked at them and ordered the price restored to ¥450,000.

lines.source: 我比較在意的是，這一下改動，接著會落到誰的手上？
lines.text: What I wonder is who would have to deal with that change next.

lines.source: 工作人員得換價牌、重排印刷物，忙到深夜仍然來不及。
lines.text: Staff had to replace the tags and redo printed materials; even working late into the night, they could not finish in time.

lines.source: 原訂隔天上午十點的記者會，於是改到下午兩點。
lines.text: The press conference, originally set for 10 a.m. the following day, was therefore moved to 2 p.m.

lines.source: 翌日，Astron正式開賣；高精度，是它要交給買家的東西。
lines.text: The next day, the Astron officially went on sale; high accuracy was what it promised its buyers.

lines.source: 精工列的月差是正負五秒，條件是在攝氏四度到三十六度的常溫範圍。
lines.text: Seiko lists a monthly accuracy of plus or minus five seconds, under normal-temperature conditions from 4 to 36 degrees Celsius.

lines.source: 你把錶從櫃台帶走以後，這個準確，會一直留在腕上嗎？
lines.text: After you took the watch away from the counter, would that accuracy stay on your wrist?

lines.source: 離開櫃台，產品卻沒有從工廠的工作清單上消失。
lines.text: The product left the counter, but it did not disappear from the factory's work list.

lines.source: 那份企業史記下，初期水晶振子老化，曾造成精度不穩。
lines.text: That company history records that aging of the early quartz resonators caused unstable accuracy.

lines.source: 開頭你擔心的返調，企業史說，許多已經售出的錶，確實又回來調整。
lines.text: As for the returns for adjustment you worried about at the start, the company history says many watches already sold did indeed come back for adjustment.

lines.source: 如果換你，最想知道的恐怕是：出門前調好了，為什麼還會變？
lines.text: If it were yours, you would probably want to know: why could it change after being adjusted before it left?

lines.source: 我反而想把目光移回做振子的那張桌；問題不只在最後那一下調整。
lines.text: I want to look back at the bench where the resonators were made; the issue went beyond that final adjustment.

lines.source: 回顧說，切削和研磨水晶片以後，表面會留下細小裂紋。
lines.text: The retrospective says cutting and grinding the quartz pieces left tiny cracks on the surface.

lines.source: 他們得處理那些裂紋，才有機會提高能用的比例。
lines.text: They had to deal with those cracks to have a chance of raising the usable proportion.

lines.source: 可是，看起來光滑的表面，就能讓人放心了嗎？
lines.text: But is a surface that looks smooth enough to put your mind at ease?

lines.source: 就算蝕去表面一層，剩下多少裂紋，也不是用眼睛看就能知道。
lines.text: Even after etching away a surface layer, you cannot tell by eye how many cracks remain.

lines.source: 想像你把振子的尖端調到所需頻率，工作到這裡還不能停。
lines.text: Imagine adjusting the resonator's tips to the required frequency; the work cannot stop there.

lines.source: 真正通電，讓它持續振動之後，裂紋狀態會變，頻率也可能跟著移動。
lines.text: Once power is actually applied and it keeps vibrating, the cracks change, and the frequency may shift too.

lines.source: 有的很快穩下來，有的卻一直沒有穩定。
lines.text: Some stabilized quickly, while others never settled down.

lines.source: 我讀到這裡才懂，調準的那一刻，還不能代替後面一段時間。
lines.text: Only when I read this did I understand: being accurate at the moment of adjustment cannot stand in for the time that follows.

lines.source: 那工廠怎麼在出貨前，先把這段變動逼出來？
lines.text: So how could the factory bring out that variation before shipping?

lines.source: 企業史記的動作，是連續通電數日，讓振子先經過老化穩定的過程。
lines.text: The company history records continuous power for several days, letting the resonators undergo aging and stabilization first.

lines.source: 每一支會變多少、變多久，都得靠經驗一點點累積。
lines.text: Experience had to build up little by little on how much each one changed, and for how long.

lines.source: 這段初期，振子的良率，回顧說只有兩成。
lines.text: In this early period, the retrospective says resonator production yield was only 20%.

lines.source: 你別把它聽成八成錶被退回；這個數字，算的是振子生產能用的比例。
lines.text: Do not read that as 80% of watches being returned; this number is the usable proportion of resonators produced.

lines.source: 如果做好的振子仍不穩，光在成品旁邊等，還能找出什麼？
lines.text: If the completed resonators were still unstable, what more could you learn just waiting beside the finished pieces?

lines.source: 這一次，得跟著管理者，走到實際加工的地方。
lines.text: This time, we need to follow the managers to where the processing actually happened.

lines.source: 加工裡有一道烘烤：把水晶片放進真空爐，用溫度去除內含的氣體。
lines.text: One processing step was baking: quartz pieces went into a vacuum furnace, where heat removed gases contained inside.

lines.source: 氣體若沒有處理好，振動頻率就可能變，時間誤差也跟著出現。
lines.text: If those gases were not properly removed, the vibration frequency could change, causing timekeeping errors too.

lines.source: 你看著爐子在運作，會先相信它已照規定加熱，還是再查設定？
lines.text: Watching the furnace run, would you assume it was heating as specified, or check the settings again?

lines.source: 開頭那座真空爐，企業史說，是管理者到現場檢查作業，才找到問題。
lines.text: As for the vacuum furnace at the start, the company history says managers found the problem only by checking operations on site.

lines.source: 設定的加熱溫度，竟然比應有的低了五十度。
lines.text: The heating temperature had actually been set 50 degrees lower than it should have been.

lines.source: 我聽到這裡，會想再找當時留下的數據：有人記下每次怎麼設嗎？
lines.text: Hearing this, I want to find the data kept at the time: did anyone record each setting?

lines.source: 回顧認為更大的問題，是設定溫度沒有作為資料記錄下來。
lines.text: The retrospective considers the bigger issue to be that the temperature settings had not been recorded as data.

lines.source: 如果換你接下一班，沒有這筆記錄，要從哪裡確認上一班做了什麼？
lines.text: If you took over the next shift without that record, where would you check what the previous shift had done?

lines.source: 這個事件讓現場檢查、留下記錄、寫明作業步驟，成了工廠要記住的教訓。
lines.text: This incident made on-site checks, records and clearly written work procedures lessons for the factory to remember.

lines.source: 不過，振子能更穩定供應，還沒有把手焊回路變得好做。
lines.text: But a steadier supply of resonators still did not make hand-soldered circuits easy to build.

lines.source: 你若想讓下一批做得更快，還能一直靠同樣數量的微小接點嗎？
lines.text: If you wanted the next batch made faster, could you keep relying on the same number of tiny contacts?

lines.source: 精工委託美國的Intersil開發低耗電晶片，要替換靠人手焊接的回路。
lines.text: Seiko commissioned the American company Intersil to develop low-power chips to replace hand-soldered circuitry.

lines.source: 企業史說，混合回路的生產性太低，成本與耗電，都還需要往下壓。
lines.text: The company history says hybrid circuits had very low productivity, and both cost and power consumption still needed to come down.

lines.source: 我比較好奇的是：既然能畫出電路，為什麼不直接換成一塊晶片？
lines.text: What I wonder is: if they could draw a circuit, why not simply replace it with a chip?

lines.source: 要畫得出來，還要真的能製造；當時這兩件事，沒有一起到位。
lines.text: They needed both the design and the ability to manufacture it; at the time, the two were not ready together.

lines.source: 另一邊，精工也開始自己建立半導體的製造能力。
lines.text: Meanwhile, Seiko also began building its own semiconductor manufacturing capability.

lines.source: 而Intersil後來送到的晶片，是不是每一顆都能照規格使用？
lines.text: And when Intersil's chips later arrived, could every one be used to specification?

lines.source: 品質與性能有差異，回顧說，當時能挑出來用的，只有約一成。
lines.text: Quality and performance varied; the retrospective says only about 10% could be selected for use at that stage.

lines.source: 你得先有可用的零件，才能談把它一批批裝進錶；不是箱子到了就解決。
lines.text: You need usable components before you can fit them into watches batch after batch; receiving a box does not solve everything.

lines.source: 你看最初上市那款Astron，後來換上外購Intersil晶片，整套電路都換了嗎？
lines.text: Look at the original Astron model: when a purchased Intersil chip was later fitted, was the entire circuit replaced?

lines.source: 沒有；企業史說，這顆CMOS專做分頻，其他電路仍採混合構成。
lines.text: No; the company history says that CMOS chip handled only frequency division, while the other circuits retained a hybrid construction.

lines.source: 這款錶改變最複雜的分頻部分後，實裝工序減少，耗電也跟著降低。
lines.text: After the most complex divider section was changed, this watch needed fewer assembly operations and consumed less power.

lines.source: 我想看的是自研這條路：原本做精密機械的人，怎麼開始做半導體？
lines.text: I want to follow the in-house path: how did people who made precision machinery begin making semiconductors?

lines.source: 企業史記下，一批年輕技術人員，從電子學和半導體基礎開始學。
lines.text: The company history records a group of young engineers starting with the basics of electronics and semiconductors.

lines.source: 他們請電子學者集中講課，也把人送進研究單位受訓。
lines.text: They invited electronics scholars to give intensive lectures and sent people to research institutions for training.

lines.source: 要理解的內容，從絕緣膜的特性，一項項往上建。
lines.text: They built their understanding step by step, starting with properties of insulating films.

lines.source: 只聽原理還不夠，拿什麼讓研究者看見，他們正在遇到的難題？
lines.text: Hearing the principles was not enough; what could they show researchers to explain the problems they were facing?

lines.source: 回顧中的山村，還把一件試作品，拿給研究半導體的垂井看。
lines.text: In the retrospective, Yamamura also took a prototype to Tarui, a semiconductor researcher.

lines.source: 他形容，那東西像個焊接出來的怪物，根本還放不進腕錶。
lines.text: He described it as a soldered monster that could not yet fit into a wristwatch.

lines.source: 但他要說明的是，團隊想從這種狀態，走向下一個層次。
lines.text: But what he wanted to convey was that the team hoped to move from that state to the next level.

lines.source: 你可以想像，小錶和眼前的大電路放在一起，差的不是換一個外殼。
lines.text: Imagine the little watch beside that large circuit; the gap would take more than a different case to close.

lines.source: 後面還有製造環境：他們把實驗室改成潔淨室，再引入半導體製造設備。
lines.text: There was also the manufacturing environment: they converted a laboratory into a cleanroom, then brought in semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

lines.source: 可是，設備進門，熟練的方法也會跟著送到嗎？
lines.text: But when equipment arrives, does manufacturing know-how come with it?

lines.source: 回顧說，缺乏製造經驗，讓他們仍得反覆實驗，事情並不順利。
lines.text: The retrospective says their lack of manufacturing experience meant repeated experiments, and progress was difficult.

lines.source: 直到一九七一年四月，企業史記下，自研A型晶片終於能按預期工作。
lines.text: It was not until April 1971, the company history records, that the in-house Type A chip finally worked as intended.

lines.source: 小於五平方毫米的面積，裝進了分頻與馬達驅動訊號輸出的功能。
lines.text: An area smaller than five square millimeters contained frequency division and motor-drive signal output functions.

lines.source: 而自研A型晶片，企業史說，用進了一九七一年十二月上市的三八系列。
lines.text: The company history says the in-house Type A chip went into the 38 series, launched in December 1971.

lines.source: 省下的電，你會拿來多用一段時間，還是換更小的電池？
lines.text: Would you use the power saved for longer running time, or for a smaller battery?

lines.source: 企業史把兩條路放在一起：維持同樣電池，就能增加使用時間。
lines.text: The company history presents both routes: keep the same battery and gain more running time.

lines.source: 如果維持原來的續航要求，就能用更小的電池，讓錶做得更薄。
lines.text: Or keep the original battery-life requirement and use a smaller battery to make the watch thinner.

lines.source: 可是，換你買下一代，遇到故障時，又還有誰能接手？
lines.text: But if you bought the next generation, who could take care of it when it failed?

lines.source: 一九七七年，安川英昭在技術論文裡，把要求寫到零售端。
lines.text: In a 1977 technical paper, Hideaki Yasukawa extended the requirements to the retail side.

lines.source: 就算出了故障，零售商也應該能靠簡單治具，做必要的修理。
lines.text: Even in the event of a failure, retailers should be able to make necessary repairs using simple jigs.

lines.source: 我想先看他留下的接法：東西越小，動手的位置是不是也變少？
lines.text: I want to look first at the connections he documented: as things get smaller, are there fewer places to work on?

lines.source: 文中舉了一款後來的高階石英錶，回路組裝先考慮了售後維護。
lines.text: The paper cites a later high-end quartz watch whose circuit assembly was designed with after-sales maintenance in mind.

lines.source: 這種回路不靠焊錫接合，改用精密沖壓、彎折與微型熔接等技術。
lines.text: That circuit used techniques such as precision stamping, bending and microwelding instead of soldered joints.

lines.source: 他特別寫到，電容與電阻這些部件，可以各自更換。
lines.text: He specifically wrote that components such as capacitors and resistors could be replaced individually.

lines.source: 如果換你碰上這個設計裡的小元件故障，就有機會只處理那個部件。
lines.text: If a small component failed in this design, you would have a chance to deal with just that component.

lines.source: 我接著想知道，這種接法到了工廠，要怎麼一批批組起來？
lines.text: Next, I want to know how those connections were assembled in batches at the factory.

lines.source: 同篇論文放了照片：回路組交給旋轉式的全自動組裝機處理。
lines.text: The same paper includes a photograph: circuit assemblies were handled by a rotary, fully automatic assembly machine.

lines.source: 文章列出的機台能力，是每月約十萬個回路單元。
lines.text: The machine capacity given in the paper was about 100,000 circuit units per month.

lines.source: 你還記得開頭那支烙鐵嗎？幾年之間，製造工具連著接法，都改了樣子。
lines.text: Remember the soldering iron at the beginning? In just a few years, both manufacturing tools and connection methods had changed.

lines.source: 不過，能組好一個回路，跟整支錶能出貨，中間還要檢查什麼？
lines.text: But between assembling a circuit and shipping a complete watch, what else needed checking?

lines.source: 安川寫的品質保證，先以每一個電子元件的可靠性為前提。
lines.text: Yasukawa's account of quality assurance starts with the reliability of every electronic component.

lines.source: 組成產品以後，還要看時間精度、運轉與顯示表現。
lines.text: Once assembled into a product, timekeeping accuracy, operation and display performance also needed examination.

lines.source: 溫度特性也在其中；你換個環境用錶，電子機構仍要面對變化。
lines.text: Temperature characteristics were part of this too; when you use your watch in a different environment, its electronic mechanism still faces changes.

lines.source: 我讀著這一頁，才會把問題從準不準，接著問到能否穩定做、方便修。
lines.text: Reading this page takes my question beyond accuracy to whether it can be made consistently and repaired easily.

lines.source: 這些後來的回路與工法，各有自己的機種，沒有同時出現在第一批錶裡。
lines.text: These later circuits and methods each belonged to their own models; they did not all appear in the first batch of watches.

lines.source: 我的答案是：準確要交到下一個人手上，還得把穩定、製造與維修一起做好。
lines.text: My answer is: to put accuracy into the next person's hands, stability, manufacturing and repair all have to be addressed too.

lines.source: 留言告訴我，你選一件新工具時，最想少操心的，是準確、維修，還是價格？
lines.text: Tell me in the comments: when you choose a new tool, what would you most like to worry less about—accuracy, repair or price?

lines.source: 想繼續看日用品如何從做得出來走到交給人用，歡迎訂閱品牌故事。
lines.text: To keep seeing how everyday objects go from something we can make to something people can use, subscribe to Brand Stories.
